label: Reply
description: Answer the caller of this run with one message: behind a Route, the whole response (status, headers, body) and the exchange ends; behind a Socket, one message and the socket stays open (status and headers refused). A file anywhere in a json body (a stored one or a url file) goes out as `{ url, mimeType, filename, sizeBytes }`, the url a link the caller fetches it from (the same link for a while, so a page that asks again keeps its video playing); sent as bytes it goes out under its own content type and filename unless `headers` sets them; `answerAs: redirect` sends the caller to the file's link.

inputs.name: body
inputs.description: Any value on json, a String on text, a stored file on bytes. A secret, or one inside it where its type says so, goes out revealed, and the run's record keeps its marker. A secret where its type declares none (inside a `JsonDict`) fails the node: declare the type so it says where the secret is.

inputs.name: answerAs
inputs.label: Answer as
inputs.description: `json`, `text` or `bytes`; empty follows the trigger's `dataType`. A GET answering a picture sets `bytes`. `redirect` (Route only) answers a file with a redirect to its link (302, or the 3xx `status` sets), so the browser fetches the file straight from where it is stored.

inputs.name: headers
inputs.description: Extra response headers (Route only); a content-type here overrides the body's. A secret value goes out revealed.

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: True once the message was handed to the caller. Absent when a Socket's message could not be made and its `whenChunkFails` skips it.

then.message: Reply '{id}' answers nobody: no trigger with a live caller (a Route, a Socket) starts a run that reaches it. Wire it from the trigger's run (through data, or `_should_flow`), or put it in a group the trigger's `_should_flow` runs.
Reply '{id}' runs after {with}, which already sent the response's head to the HTTP caller, so this answer can never go out. To end the exchange after a stream, use a Close.
